In [[nonlinear control]], '''Aizerman's conjecture''' or '''Aizerman problem''' states that a linear system in feedback with a sector nonlinearity would be stable if the linear system is stable for any linear gain of the sector. This conjecture, proposed by Mark Aronovich Aizerman in 1949,<ref>{{cite book | chapter-url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/10.1142/9789812799852_0006 | doi=10.1142/9789812799852_0006 | chapter=The Aizerman conjecture: The Popov method | title=Mathematical Problems of Control Theory | series=Series on Stability, Vibration and Control of Systems, Series A | date=2001 | volume=6 | pages=155–166 | publisher=World Scientific | isbn=978-981-02-4694-5 }}</ref> was proven false but led to the (valid) [[Nonlinear control#Absolute stability problem|sufficient criteria on absolute stability]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Liberzon |first=M. R. |date=2006 |title=Essays on the absolute stability theory |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1134/S0005117906100043 |journal=Automation and Remote Control |language=en |volume=67 |issue=10 |pages=1610–1644 |doi=10.1134/S0005117906100043 |s2cid=120434924 |issn=0005-1179|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Mathematical statement of Aizerman's conjecture (Aizerman problem)==
''Consider a system with one scalar nonlinearity''
:<math>
  \frac{dx}{dt}=Px+qf(e),\quad e=r^*x \quad x\in\mathbb R^n,
</math>
''where P is a constant n×n-matrix, q, r are constant n-dimensional vectors, ∗ is an operation of transposition, f(e) is scalar function, and f(0)=0. Suppose that the nonlinearity f is sector bounded, meaning that for some real'' <math>
 k_1
</math> and <math>
 k_2
</math> with <math>
 k_1 <k_2
</math>, the function <math>
 f
</math> satisfies
:<math>
 k_1  < \frac{f(e)}{e}< k_2, \quad \forall \; e \neq 0.
</math>
''Then Aizerman's conjecture is that the system is stable in large (i.e. unique stationary point is global [[attractor]]) if all linear systems with f(e)=ke, k ∈(k1,k2) are asymptotically stable.''

There are counterexamples to Aizerman's conjecture such that nonlinearity belongs to the sector of linear stability and unique stable equilibrium coexists with a stable periodic solution, i.e. a [[hidden oscillation]].<ref name=2011-DAN-Kalman>{{cite journal
 |author1=Leonov G.A. |author2=Kuznetsov N.V. | year = 2011
 | title = Algorithms for Searching for Hidden Oscillations in the Aizerman and Kalman Problems
 | journal = Doklady Mathematics
 | volume = 84
 | number = 1
 | pages = 475–481
 | url = http://www.math.spbu.ru/user/nk/PDF/2011-DAN-Absolute-stability-Aizerman-problem-Kalman-conjecture.pdf
 | doi = 10.1134/S1064562411040120|s2cid=120692391 }}
</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 |author1=Bragin V.O. |author2=Vagaitsev V.I. |author3=Kuznetsov N.V. |author4=Leonov G.A. | year = 2011
 | title = Algorithms for Finding Hidden Oscillations in Nonlinear Systems. The Aizerman and Kalman Conjectures and Chua's Circuits
 | journal = Journal of Computer and Systems Sciences International
 | volume = 50
 | number = 5
 | pages = 511–543
 | url = http://www.math.spbu.ru/user/nk/PDF/2011-TiSU-Hidden-oscillations-attractors-Aizerman-Kalman-conjectures.pdf
 | doi = 10.1134/S106423071104006X|s2cid=21657305 }}
</ref><ref name=2020-TiSU-Kalman>{{cite journal | 
  author1=Kuznetsov N.V. | 
  year = 2020| 
  title = Theory of hidden oscillations and stability of control systems| 
 journal = Journal of Computer and Systems Sciences International| 
 volume = 59| number = 5|pages = 647&ndash;668| 
 url = https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1134/S1064230720050093.pdf|
 doi = 10.1134/S1064230720050093| 
 s2cid = 225304463}}
</ref><ref name=2011-IJBC-Hidden-attractors>{{cite journal |author1=Leonov G.A. |author2=Kuznetsov N.V. | 
year = 2013 | 
title = Hidden attractors in dynamical systems. From hidden oscillations in Hilbert-Kolmogorov, Aizerman, and Kalman problems to hidden chaotic attractor in Chua circuits | 
journal = International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos | 
volume = 23 | 
issue = 1 | 
pages = 1330002–219|
doi = 10.1142/S0218127413300024|bibcode=2013IJBC...2330002L | 
doi-access =  }}
</ref> However, under stronger assumptions on the system, such as positivity, Aizerman's conjecture is known to hold true.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Drummond |first1=Ross |last2=Guiver |first2=Chris |last3=Turner |first3=Matthew C. |date=2023 |title=Aizerman Conjectures for a Class of Multivariate Positive Systems |journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control |volume=68 |issue=8 |pages=5073–5080 |doi=10.1109/TAC.2022.3217740 |bibcode=2023ITAC...68.5073D |s2cid=260255282 |issn=0018-9286|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Variants ==

* Strengthening of Aizerman's conjecture is [[Kalman's conjecture]] (or [[Kalman's conjecture|Kalman problem]]) where in place of condition on the nonlinearity it is required that the derivative of nonlinearity belongs to linear stability sector.
* A multivariate version of Aizerman's conjecture holds true over the complex field,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hinrichsen |first1=D. |last2=Pritchard |first2=A. J. |date=1992-01-01 |title=Destabilization by output feedback |journal=Differential and Integral Equations |volume=5 |issue=2 |doi=10.57262/die/1371043976 |s2cid=118359120 |issn=0893-4983|doi-access=free }}</ref> and it can be used to derive the [[circle criterion]] for the stability of nonlinear time-varying systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jayawardhana |first1=Bayu |last2=Logemann |first2=Hartmut |last3=Ryan |first3=Eugene |date=2011 |title=The Circle Criterion and Input-to-State Stability |journal=IEEE Control Systems Magazine |volume=31 |issue=4 |pages=32–67 |doi=10.1109/MCS.2011.941143 |s2cid=84839719 |issn=1066-033X}}</ref>
